Mining's Impact

How resource extraction affects our planet

🎯 LEARNING INTENTION

We are learning to evaluate the environmental impact of mining

✓ SUCCESS CRITERIA

🌍 REAL WORLD LINK

Mining Powers Modern Life

But at what cost to the environment?

Steel in buildings, aluminium in cans, and coal for electricity all come from mining — which can cause long-lasting impacts on land, water, and air.

MINING IMPACTS

Open-Cut Mining: Digging In

Removes vegetation and topsoil over the mined area
Alters landforms and habitats for plants and animals
Can create pits, dust and noise pollution
WATER POLLUTION

Acid Mine Drainage

Tailings are fine residues left after processing; waste rock is not processed
Acid drainage can form when exposed sulfide minerals react with air and water
Acidic water can mobilise metals into streams and groundwater
MINE SITE IMPACTS

Other Impacts at the Mine Site

Water is used in ore processing; requirements vary by mine and method
Dust can affect local air quality
Roads and machinery can disturb surrounding areas
AIR POLLUTION

Burning Coal: Impacts in the Air

Burning coal releases CO₂, a greenhouse gas
It can also release SO₂ and fine particles, which affect air quality
CO₂ contributes to warming by trapping heat in the atmosphere
CARBON FOOTPRINT

Steel and Aluminium: Hidden Footprint

Iron and steel production is responsible for roughly 7–9% of global CO₂ emissions
Aluminium smelting is electricity-intensive; emissions depend strongly on the electricity source
Coal-powered electricity increases aluminium's greenhouse-gas emissions

Benefits vs Environmental Costs

💰 Economic
Jobs and income for communities
Materials for buildings, transport
Export revenue for Australia
🌿 Environment
Habitat loss and soil destruction
Water and air pollution
CO₂ emissions drive climate change
RESTORATION

Rehabilitation: Fixing the Damage

Mine approvals commonly require rehabilitation planning and monitoring
Exact requirements vary by jurisdiction and project approval
Recovery can take decades and may not recreate the original ecosystem
